en: Sutta Nipāta 5.4 Puṇṇakamāṇavapucchā “To the one who sees the root, the immovable— ”
(Thus spoke the Venerable Puṇṇaka:
"I have come with a question:
On what do the seers among men depend?"
Khattiyas and brahmins have performed various sacrifices here in the world for the sake of the deities;
I ask you, Blessed One, please tell me this.
“Whatever sages there may be among these humans,
O Puṇṇaka,” said the Blessed One,
“whether they be khattiyas, brahmins, or deities;”
Many here in the world have performed sacrifices,
Puṇṇaka, hoping for this very state;
yearning for old age, they have performed sacrifices.
“Whatever sages there are among these humans—
whether kshatriyas, brahmins, or deities,” (said the Venerable Puṇṇaka).
Many have performed sacrifices here in the world;
O Blessed One, were they diligent on the path of sacrifice?
Did they, O Noble One, cross over birth and old age?
“I ask you, Blessed One, tell me this.
“They hope, they praise, they long for,
they sacrifice,” said the Blessed One, “Puṇṇaka.”
Depending on gain, they long for sensual pleasures;
devoted to sacrifice and stained by passion for existence,
they have not transcended birth and old age— so I say.
“If those engaged in sacrifice have not transcended birth and old age by means of their offerings, O venerable sir,” (said the Venerable Puṇṇaka).
Now who indeed in the world of gods and humans,
O Blessed One, has crossed over birth and old age? I ask you, tell me that.
“Having discerned the high and low in the world,
O Puṇṇaka (said the Blessed One),
he for whom there is no wavering anywhere in the world;”
“Holy, smokeless, free from distress, and desireless—he has crossed over birth and old age; this is what I say.
This was the third inquiry of the young man Puṇṇaka.
